audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim national assembly, Benjamin confrontation, three battles, Gibeah ambush, and near-destruction of Benjamin narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for all-Israel mobilization, Levite's self-protective testimony, absence of the murdered woman's voice, demand for perpetrators, Benjamin's collective refusal, troop figures, left-handed slingers, repeated YHWH inquiries, catastrophic Israelite losses, Phinehas and ark chronology, ambush tactics, Gibeah destruction, pursuit to Rimmon, massacre totals, killing across Benjaminite towns, animals, and city burning.

verses.restored: All children of Israel went out, and congregation gathered as one man, from Dan to Beersheba and land of Gilead, to YHWH at Mizpah.

familiar.text: Then all the children of Israel went out, and the congregation was gathered together as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, unto the LORD in Mizpeh.

modern.text: Then all the Israelites from Dan to Beersheba and from the land of Gilead came out, and the congregation assembled as one man before the LORD at Mizpah.

modern.text: The leaders of all the people and all the tribes of Israel presented themselves in the assembly of God’s people: 400,000 men on foot, armed with swords.

modern.text: (Meanwhile the Benjamites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah.) And the Israelites asked, “Tell us, how did this wicked thing happen?”

verses.restored: The Levite, man of woman who had been murdered, answered and said, I came to Gibeah that belongs to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to lodge.

familiar.text: And the Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, answered and said, I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to lodge.

modern.text: So the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered: “I and my concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.

familiar.text: And the men of Gibeah rose against me, and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me: and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead.

modern.text: And during the night, the men of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house. They intended to kill me, but they abused my concubine, and she died.

modern.text: Then I took my concubine, cut her into pieces, and sent her throughout the land of Israel’s inheritance, because they had committed a lewd and disgraceful act in Israel.

verses.restored: We will take ten men of a hundred from all tribes of Israel, and a hundred of a thousand, and a thousand of ten thousand, to take provisions for people, so that when they come to Gibeah of Benjamin they may do to it according to all outrage it has done in Israel.

familiar.text: And we will take ten men of an hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, and an hundred of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to fetch victual for the people, that they may do, when they come to Gibeah of Benjamin, according to all the folly that they have wrought in Israel.

modern.text: We will take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to supply provisions for the army when they go to Gibeah in Benjamin to punish them for the atrocity they have committed in Israel.”

modern.text: Hand over the wicked men of Gibeah so we can put them to death and purge Israel of this evil.” But the Benjamites refused to heed the voice of their fellow Israelites.

modern.text: The Israelites set out, went up to Bethel, and inquired of God, “Who of us shall go up first to fight against the Benjamites?” “Judah will be first,” the LORD replied.

verses.restored: Children of Benjamin went out to meet the people and were drawn away from city. They began to strike some of people dead as time after time on highways, one of which goes up to Bethel and one to Gibeah in field, about thirty men of Israel.

familiar.text: And the children of Benjamin went out against the people, and were drawn away from the city; and they began to smite of the people, and kill, as at other times, in the highways, of which one goeth up to the house of God, and the other to Gibeah in the field, about thirty men of Israel.

modern.text: The Benjamites came out against them and were drawn away from the city. They began to attack the people as before, killing about thirty men of Israel in the fields and on the roads, one of which led up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah.

modern.text: “We are defeating them as before,” said the Benjamites. But the Israelites said, “Let us retreat and draw them away from the city onto the roads.”

verses.restored: Ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came opposite Gibeah, and battle was heavy. Benjamin did not know that disaster was touching them.

familiar.text: And there came against Gibeah ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and the battle was sore: but they knew not that evil was near them.

modern.text: Then 10,000 select men from all Israel made a frontal assault against Gibeah, and the battle was fierce. But the Benjamites did not realize that disaster was upon them.

modern.text: The LORD defeated Benjamin in the presence of Israel, and on that day the Israelites slaughtered 25,100 Benjamites, all armed with swords.

familiar.text: So the children of Benjamin saw that they were smitten: for the men of Israel gave place to the Benjamites, because they trusted unto the liers in wait which they had set beside Gibeah.

modern.text: Then the Benjamites realized they had been defeated. Now the men of Israel had retreated before Benjamin because they were relying on the ambush they had set against Gibeah.

modern.text: Then the men of Israel turned back on them, and the men of Benjamin were terrified when they realized that disaster had come upon them.

modern.text: They surrounded the Benjamites, pursued them, and easily overtook them in the vicinity of Gibeah on the east.

modern.text: Then the Benjamites turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and Israel cut down 5,000 men on the roads. And they overtook them at Gidom and struck down 2,000 more.

verses.restored: Men of Israel returned to children of Benjamin and struck them by edge of sword, from inhabited city to animal to all that was found. Also all cities that were found they sent into fire.

familiar.text: And the men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin, and smote them with the edge of the sword, as well the men of every city, as the beast, and all that came to hand: also they set on fire all the cities that they came to.

modern.text: And the men of Israel turned back against the other Benjamites and put to the sword all the cities, including the animals and everything else they found. And they burned down all the cities in their path.

original.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל שָׁ֣בוּ אֶל בְּנֵ֤י בִנְיָמִן֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּם לְפִי חֶ֔רֶב מֵעִ֤יר מְתֹם֙ עַד בְּהֵמָ֔ה עַ֖ד כָּל הַנִּמְצָ֑א גַּ֛ם כָּל הֶעָרִ֥ים הַנִּמְצָא֖וֹת שִׁלְּח֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ

translation_notes: The national assembly forms around the Levite's circulated body parts, but the murdered woman remains unnamed and cannot testify. His account omits that he himself seized and surrendered her and later dismembered her body. Public testimony must be evaluated for self-exoneration and missing survivor voice.

The demand in verse 13 targets perpetrators in Gibeah, but Benjamin's refusal converts criminal accountability into tribal solidarity. Protecting abusers because they belong to one's own group deepens harm; it does not make collective extermination just.
Calling violent offenders 'sons of beliyyaal' is an ancient idiom for lawlessness, not a claim that any people are ontologically worthless or beyond human dignity.

The large troop and casualty figures may reflect epic or schematic historiography and require later textual and historical audit. Whatever their scale, the narrative presents catastrophic Israelite-on-Israelite bloodshed.
The seven hundred left-handed or right-hand-restricted slingers are praised for skill. Bodily difference is not defect, shame, or evidence of moral danger.

Israel repeatedly inquires of YHWH and receives battle directions, yet suffers enormous losses and ultimately commits near-extermination. Oracle language inside this tragic narrative may not be abstracted into permission for religious war, certainty about violence, or claims that victory proves righteousness.
The presence of Phinehas and the ark creates chronological and compositional questions within Judges. Later audit should not flatten these traditions into a simple modern war chronology.
The third battle uses deliberate retreat, ambush, fire, and a smoke signal. Tactical description is not moral endorsement or instruction for vigilantism.

Verse 35 attributes Benjamin's defeat to YHWH, while surrounding verses explain the ambush. Theological causation and human military action coexist in the narrative; neither erases responsibility for what follows.
The pursuit continues after the battlefield collapse and kills fleeing Benjaminites. Only six hundred reach Rimmon. Refusal of surrender or restraint turns punishment into tribal destruction.
Verse 48 extends violence from combatants to settlements, inhabitants, animals, property, and fire. This is collective punishment and near-genocide, not justice for the woman harmed at Gibeah.

The chapter's stated goal of removing evil ends by multiplying death and destroying communities. Justice that abandons proportionality, survivors, civilians, and future life becomes another form of the outrage it claims to answer.
safety_note: Maximum anti-tribal-violence and anti-genocide safeguards: Do not use Divine inquiry, majority unity, perpetrator-protection, military loss, or victory to sanctify collective punishment. Benjaminite civilians, fugitives, animals, homes, and future generations are not legitimate substitutes for accountable perpetrators. Do not glorify civil war, ambush, burning cities, extermination, or retaliation as survivor justice. The murdered woman's body must not be used again to recruit hatred against an ethnicity, tribe, religion, gender, sexuality, or modern population.
